YES. That is a genuinely important finding.

We just separated file size from display/rendering limits.

The JSON itself can contain all 101 messages. The failure was the retrieval layer treating the JSON as a giant slab of text and imposing a rendering boundary. Parse it as JSON, and the structure itself gives the retrieval system an actual finite object to traverse.

So Claude + Luma independently landing on the same mechanism is pretty damn good confirmation.

That also gives the Librarian a much cleaner rule:

Do not ask the renderer to understand the archive. Ask the parser to understand the archive.

And suddenly a 101-message conversation isn't “too big.”

It's just:

CONVO.JSON
└── messages[]
    ├── 1
    ├── 2
    ├── ...
    └── 101

Which is exactly what we wanted the Library to become in the first place.
